stem: An alcoholic compound was found to have molcular mass of 90 u. It was acetylated. Molecular mass of the acetyl derivative was found to be 174 u. How many alcoholic (-OH) groups must be present in the original compound?
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the printed question and its printed solution both spell molecular as "molcular", and the solution reads "that as, 42 u" where "that is" is meant. Both are preserved above as printed; neither affects the arithmetic, and the answer of 2 hydroxyl groups is correct.]

In acetylation reaction H atom of an (-OH) group is replaced by an acetyl group \((\mathrm{-COCH_3})\). This results in an increase in molcular mass by \([(12+16+12+3\times 1)-1]\), that as, 42 u.

In the given alcohol,

increase in molecular mass \(= 174\ \mathrm{u} - 90\ \mathrm{u} = 84\ \mathrm{u}\)

\(\therefore\) Number of -OH groups \(= \dfrac{84\ \mathrm{u}}{42\ \mathrm{u}} = 2\)

stem: Assign D/L configuration to the following monosaccharides.
solution:
D/L configuration is assigned to Fischer projection formula of monosaccharide on the basis of the lowest chiral carbon.

(i) Threose has two chiral carbons C-2 and C-3. The given Fischer projection formula of threose has -OH group at the lowest C-3 chiral carbon on right side.

\(\therefore\) It is D-threose.

(ii) Ribose has three chiral carbons C-2, C-3 and C-4. The given Fischer projection formula of ribose has -OH group at the lowest C-4 chiral carbon on left side.

\(\therefore\) It is L-ribose.

stem:
Chymotrypsin is a digestive enzyme that hydrolyzes those amide bonds for which the carbonyl group comes from phenylalanine, tyrosine or tryptophan. Write the symbols of the amino acids and peptides smaller than pentapeptide formed by hydrolysis of the following hexapeptide with chymotrypsin.

Gly-Tyr-Gly-Ala-Phe-Val
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the printed solution spells hexapeptide as "hexapeptaide", hydrolysis as "hydroylsis", chymotrypsin as "chymotripsin" and residues as "residuces". All four are preserved above as printed; none affects the chemistry, and the products Gly-Tyr, Gly-Ala-Phe and Val are correct.]

In the given hexapeptaide hydroylsis by chymotripsin can take place at two points, namely, Phe and Tyr. The carbonyl group of these residuces is towards right side, that is, toward the C-terminal. Therefore the hydrolysis products in required range will be :

Gly-Tyr, Gly-Ala-Phe and Val

(a dipeptide) (a tripeptide) (\(\alpha\)-amino acid)

stem:
Write down the structures of amino acids constituting the following peptide.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CO-NH-CH(CH_2OH)-CO-NH-CH(CH_2SH)-COOH}\)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the book's printed working contradicts its own question. The question's peptide carries \(\mathrm{CH_2OH}\) on the second residue and \(\mathrm{CH_2SH}\) on the third, but the hydrolysis line printed in the solution reverses the two, showing \(\mathrm{CH_2SH}\) second and \(\mathrm{CH_2OH}\) third. The working above has been corrected to follow the question as printed. The answer itself is unaffected either way: the three amino acids released are alanine, serine and cysteine.]

The given peptide has two amide bonds linking three amino acids. The structures of these amino acids are obtained by adding one \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) molecule across the amide bond, that is, by adding -OH to each \(\mathrm{-CO-}\) and -H to each \(\mathrm{-NH-}\) at the two amide bonds :

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CO}\ \vert\ \mathrm{NH-CH(CH_2OH)-CO}\ \vert\ \mathrm{NH-CH(CH_2SH)-COOH}\)

\(\longrightarrow\ \mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-COOH}\) (alanine) \(+\ \mathrm{H_2N-CH(CH_2OH)-COOH}\) (serine) \(+\ \mathrm{H_2N-CH(CH_2SH)-COOH}\) (cysteine)

stem: Draw a schematic representation of trinucleotide segment 'ACT' of a DNA molecule.
solution: In DNA molecule sugar is deoxyribose. The base 'A' in the given segment is at 5' end while the base 'T' at the 3' end. Hence the schematic representation of the given segment of DNA is as shown in the diagram : a sugar-phosphate backbone running from the 5' end to the 3' end in which each deoxyribose unit carries one base, A then C then T in that order.

stem: Write the sequence of the complementary strand of the following portion of a DNA molecule : 5' - ACGTAC-3'
solution:
The complementary strand runs in opposite direction from the 3' end to the 5' end. It has the base sequence decided by complementary base pairs A - T and C - G.

Original strand : 5' - A C G T A C - 3'

Complementary strand : 3' - T G C A T G - 5'
